discovery: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies (WMAP), establishing the standard cosmological model and its parameters
motivation: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe, led by Bennett with Page and Spergel as central architects of its instrument and analysis, turned cosmology into a precision science. Its full-sky maps of the CMB temperature and polarization anisotropies measured the age, geometry and composition of the universe to percent precision. They confirmed spatial flatness and the acoustic-peak structure, gave independent evidence for dark energy that agreed with the supernova results, pinned down the baryon and dark matter densities, detected the early reionization of the universe, and measured a near-scale-invariant, slightly red-tilted primordial spectrum, a key signature consistent with inflation. WMAP's six-parameter ΛCDM became the reference model against which every other measurement, including the local expansion rate, is now tested. This was careful, systematics-controlled measurement that changed fundamental physics, and it set the stage for Planck and the present search for cracks in the standard model.
